lineage.vibe: Create the inventory domain with the following products: stock_position, lot_batch, inventory_storage_location, stock_movement, inventory_replenishment_order, inventory_cycle_count, safety_stock_policy, intransit_shipment, oos_event, stock_hold, recall_event, inventory_vmi_agreement, stock_valuation, stock_adjustment, reservation, warehouse.
lineage.interpretation: Define inventory domain and its products

became.before: Transactional record tracking inventory that is physically in-transit between nodes in the distribution network (supplier-to-DC, DC-to-DC, DC-to-store). Captures shipment reference, origin node, destination node, carrier, in-transit quantity by SKU/lot, expected arrival date, actual arrival date, in-transit status (departed, in-transit, arrived, exception), and OTIF flag. Provides multi-echelon inventory visibility for in-transit stock that is not yet receipted at destination.

Transactional record of physical inventory cycle count events conducted at storage locations. Captures count date, count method (full physical, ABC cycle, perpetual), counted quantity, system quantity, variance quantity, variance percentage, count status (planned, in-progress, confirmed, posted), and approver. Supports inventory accuracy KPIs, shrinkage investigation triggers, and WMS reconciliation. Distinct from stock_movement as it represents a formal audit event, not a stock transaction.
became.after: Cycle count activities for inventory accuracy

became.before: Transactional record of inventory replenishment requests and orders generated through VMI auto-replenishment, distribution requirements planning (DRP), or manual triggers. Captures replenishment type, requested quantity, approved quantity, source location, destination location, requested delivery date, priority, and fulfillment status. Closes the loop between demand sensing signals and physical stock movement execution.

Master record for physical and logical storage locations within the distribution network including distribution centers, warehouses, retail back-rooms, 3PL facilities, and in-transit staging areas. Captures location code, location type (bulk, pick, reserve, quarantine, returns), temperature zone, capacity (weight, volume, pallet positions), WMS zone mapping, and geo-coordinates. Serves as the single source of truth for the location hierarchy used across warehouse management and inventory systems.

Master record defining Vendor Managed Inventory (VMI) agreements between Consumer Goods and its retail/distributor customers. Captures VMI partner (retailer/distributor), covered SKUs, min/max stock levels at partner location, replenishment frequency, data sharing method (EDI, TradeEdge), service level commitment, VMI start date, VMI end date, and agreement status. Distinct from replenishment_order (the execution) — this is the governing policy for VMI-managed inventory relationships.

Master record for each manufactured or received lot/batch of a SKU, capturing batch number, manufacturing date, expiry date, best-before date, country of origin, GMP status, and quarantine flags. Supports FEFO/FIFO rotation enforcement, lot-level traceability for recall readiness, and regulatory compliance (FDA 21 CFR Part 11, EU REACH, EU Food Information Regulation). Linked to production batch records in manufacturing execution systems and quality inspection lots.
became.after: Lot and batch tracking for inventory traceability

became.before: Transactional record capturing Out-of-Stock (OOS) and On-Shelf Availability (OSA) events at the SKU-location level. Captures OOS start timestamp, OOS end timestamp, OOS duration (hours), root cause category (demand spike, replenishment failure, forecast miss, upstream stockout, logistics delay), estimated lost sales value, and resolution action. Sourced from POS data feeds and demand sensing signals. Critical for OSA improvement programs, retail execution accountability, and service level reporting.

Master record for product recall and withdrawal events triggered by safety, quality, or regulatory findings. Captures recall classification (Class I/II/III FDA, voluntary withdrawal), affected SKUs, affected lot/batch ranges, recall scope (geographic, channel, customer), recall initiation date, regulatory notification date (FDA/CPSC), quantity recalled, quantity recovered, recall status, and financial impact estimate. Supports lot_batch traceability queries and regulatory reporting obligations.
became.after: Product recall events and affected inventory

became.before: Transactional record of inventory reservations that earmark specific stock quantities for confirmed sales orders, production orders, promotional commitments, or intercompany transfers. Captures reservation type (sales order, production, promotional, intercompany), reserved quantity, reserved lot/batch (if FEFO-specific), reservation date, expiry date of reservation, fulfillment status, and consuming document reference. Prevents double-allocation of available stock across competing demand streams.
became.after: Inventory reservations for orders and allocations

became.before: Master record defining safety stock parameters and reorder point policies for each SKU-location combination. Captures safety stock quantity, reorder point, maximum stock level, minimum order quantity (MOQ), replenishment lead time, service level target (%), demand variability coefficient, and policy review date. Feeds SAP IBP inventory optimization and DRP planning runs. Distinct from stock_position (actual balance) — this is the policy/rule that governs when replenishment is triggered.
became.after: Safety stock policies by SKU and location

became.before: Transactional record of manual and system-generated inventory adjustments that correct stock balances outside of normal goods movement flows. Captures adjustment reason (shrinkage, damage, system reconciliation, theft, sampling, promotional giveaway), adjusted quantity, adjusted value, adjustment date, approver, and supporting reference document. Distinct from stock_movement (which covers standard GR/GI flows) — adjustments represent exception corrections to the inventory ledger.

Transactional record of quality holds, regulatory blocks, and commercial holds placed on inventory lots or stock positions. Captures hold type (QC inspection hold, regulatory recall hold, commercial dispute hold, damage hold), hold reason, hold quantity, hold start date, hold release date, hold status, approving authority, and disposition decision (release, rework, destroy, return to supplier). Integrates with quality management usage decisions and regulatory hold workflows.
became.after: Inventory holds for quality or regulatory reasons

became.before: Transactional record of every inventory movement event including goods receipts, goods issues, stock transfers, returns, write-offs, and inter-plant transfers. Captures movement type code, quantity, unit of measure, source and destination locations, posting date, reference document (purchase order, production order, delivery note), carrier/shipment reference for inter-node transfers, and posting user. Provides the full audit trail for inventory reconciliation and in-transit tracking.

Core master record of physical inventory on-hand quantities for each SKU at each storage location. Captures unrestricted, quality-hold, blocked, consignment, VMI-managed, and in-transit stock quantities by stock type and special stock indicator. Serves as the authoritative real-time inventory balance (single source of truth for quantity on hand). Supports OOS/OSA monitoring, days-inventory-outstanding calculation, available-to-promise derivation, and multi-echelon inventory visibility across the distribution network.
became.after: Current inventory position by SKU, location, and lot/batch

became.before: Transactional record of inventory valuation snapshots for each SKU-location combination, capturing standard cost, moving average price, total stock value, COGS allocation, inventory write-down amounts, and valuation method (standard cost, FIFO, weighted average). Aligned with material ledger postings in the financial system. Supports COGS reporting, days-inventory-outstanding calculation, and financial close processes. Distinct from stock_position (quantity) — this captures the monetary value dimension of inventory.
Master reference table for warehouse. Referenced by warehouse_id.

before.description: Actual date and time when the shipment physically arrived at the destination node. Null until arrival occurs. Used for OTIF performance measurement.
Production batch identifier for granular traceability within a lot. Used for quality assurance and regulatory compliance.
Identifier of the logistics carrier or third-party logistics provider (3PL) responsible for transporting the shipment.
The transportation service level or speed tier selected for this shipment, impacting transit time and cost.
Actual date and time when the shipment physically departed from the origin node. Used for transit time calculation and OTIF (On Time In Full) measurement.
Identifier of the target location in the distribution network where the shipment is being delivered (distribution center, warehouse, retail store, or customer location).
Classification of the destination location type in the supply chain network.
Detailed narrative description of the exception event, including root cause and resolution actions taken.
Boolean indicator of whether the shipment encountered any exceptions during transit (delays, damage, routing issues, temperature excursions).
Classification of the primary exception encountered during shipment transit. Null if no exception occurred.
Total freight transportation cost for this shipment in the base currency. Used for logistics cost allocation and freight audit.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the freight cost amount.
DOT hazard class code for hazardous materials (e.g., 3 for flammable liquids, 8 for corrosives). Null if not hazmat.
Boolean indicator of whether the shipment contains hazardous materials requiring special handling, labeling, and regulatory compliance.
Boolean indicator of whether the shipment arrived with the complete expected quantity, regardless of timing.
Total quantity of inventory units currently in-transit for this shipment. Represents stock that has left origin but not yet arrived at destination.
Date and time when this in-transit shipment record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking and data freshness monitoring.
Manufacturing lot or batch number for traceability and recall readiness. Critical for FEFO (First Expired First Out) rotation and quality control.
Boolean indicator of whether the shipment arrived on or before the expected arrival date, regardless of quantity accuracy.
Foreign key linking to sales.order. Business justification: Required for shipment‑to‑order tracking in OTIF logistics reports; sales order is the business driver for each in‑transit shipment.
Classification of the origin location type in the supply chain network.
Boolean indicator of whether the shipment met OTIF performance criteria (arrived on time with full quantity). True if both time and quantity targets were met.
Number of pallets included in this shipment. Used for warehouse receiving planning and dock scheduling.
Identifier of the source location in the distribution network from which the shipment departed (supplier facility, distribution center, warehouse, or manufacturing plant).
Purchase order number associated with this shipment, linking the in-transit inventory to the originating procurement transaction.
Unit of measure for the in-transit quantity (each, case, pallet, weight, volume). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: each|case|pallet|kg|lbs|liter|gallon — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

Date and time when the shipment was formally receipted into destination inventory through WMS (Warehouse Management System). May differ from arrival timestamp due to inspection and put-away processes.
Maximum acceptable temperature in Celsius for temperature-controlled shipments. Used for cold chain compliance monitoring.
Minimum acceptable temperature in Celsius for temperature-controlled shipments. Used for cold chain compliance monitoring.

Foreign key linking to research.research_formulation. Business justification: Launch logistics report tracks shipments of newly launched formulations, tying in‑transit data to the formulation for rollout monitoring.
External business identifier for the shipment, used for tracking and communication with carriers and logistics partners. May be ASN (Advanced Shipping Notice) number or BOL (Bill of Lading) number.
Total volume of the shipment in cubic meters. Used for transportation capacity planning and dimensional weight calculations.
Total gross weight of the shipment in kilograms, including packaging. Used for freight cost calculation and carrier capacity planning.
Boolean indicator of whether this shipment requires temperature-controlled transportation (cold chain logistics) to maintain product quality and safety.
Number of calendar days the shipment was in transit from departure to arrival. Calculated as the difference between actual arrival and departure timestamps.
Primary mode of transportation used for moving the shipment between origin and destination.
The ABC inventory classification of the SKU at the time of count. A = high-value items counted frequently, B = medium-value, C = low-value counted less frequently. Drives cycle count frequency.
The ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) document number or transaction ID generated when the inventory adjustment was posted. Used for financial audit trail and reconciliation.
Indicates whether the variance has been posted as an inventory adjustment in the ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) system. True = adjustment posted, False = pending posting.
Date and time when the cycle count was approved by the authorized supervisor. Part of the audit trail for inventory adjustments.
Identifier of the supervisor or manager who approved the cycle count results and authorized the variance adjustment. Required for SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) compliance and segregation of duties.

The methodology used for the cycle count. Full physical = complete inventory audit, ABC cycle = frequency-based counting by value classification, perpetual = continuous counting, spot check = random verification, blind count = counter does not see system quantity.
The warehouse zone or area designation where the count took place (e.g., receiving, picking, reserve, quarantine). Used for zone-based cycle count scheduling.
The expiration or best-before date of the lot/batch counted. Critical for FEFO (First Expired First Out) rotation rules and consumer safety in CPG (Consumer Packaged Goods).
The total monetary value of the counted inventory based on the counted quantity and the unit cost at the time of count. Used for financial reconciliation and shrinkage cost calculation.
Date and time when the cycle count record was last updated. Tracks changes through the count lifecycle (planned → in_progress → confirmed → posted).
Manufacturing lot or batch number of the inventory counted. Critical for traceability and recall readiness in consumer goods.
Identifier of the warehouse or distribution center where the cycle count was performed. Supports multi-site inventory management.
If this is a recount, references the inventory_cycle_count_id of the original count that triggered the recount requirement. Null for initial counts.
Identifier of the warehouse associate or employee who performed the physical count. Used for accountability and performance tracking.
Indicates whether the counted inventory is in quarantine status pending quality inspection or regulatory clearance. True = quarantined, False = available.
Indicates whether this cycle count is a recount of a previous count that exceeded variance thresholds. True = recount, False = initial count.
Indicates whether the counted inventory is stored in a temperature-controlled environment. True = cold chain storage, False = ambient. Relevant for perishable consumer goods.
Free-text explanation or additional context provided by the counter or approver regarding the variance. Used for investigation and documentation.

Categorization of the root cause for the inventory variance. Used for shrinkage analysis, process improvement, and loss prevention. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: shrinkage|damage|misplacement|system_error|receiving_error|picking_error|expiration|theft|administrative_error|vendor_shortage — promote to reference product]

The monetary value of the variance (variance_quantity * unit_cost). Represents the financial impact of the inventory discrepancy. Used for shrinkage reporting and P&L (Profit and Loss) impact analysis.
Actual date the shipment was received at the destination location. Used to measure delivery performance and OTIF compliance.
Actual date the shipment departed from the source location. Used to calculate On Time In Full (OTIF) performance.
Quantity of the SKU approved for fulfillment after review and Available to Promise (ATP) validation. May differ from requested quantity due to supply constraints.

Foreign key linking to marketing.campaign. Business justification: Promotional campaigns trigger dedicated replenishment orders; linking enables the Campaign‑Driven Replenishment Report used in trade spend planning.
Explanation for why the replenishment order was cancelled, if applicable. Examples include demand change, supply constraint, or duplicate order.
Reference to the logistics carrier assigned to transport this replenishment shipment from source to destination.

Total quantity of product subject to the recall action. May differ from quantity distributed if recall scope is narrowed to specific lots, channels, or geographies.

affected_objects.before: Transactional record tracking inventory that is physically in-transit between nodes in the distribution network (supplier-to-DC, DC-to-DC, DC-to-store). Captures shipment reference, origin node, destination node, carrier, in-transit quantity by SKU/lot, expected arrival date, actual arrival date, in-transit status (departed, in-transit, arrived, exception), and OTIF flag. Provides multi-echelon inventory visibility for in-transit stock that is not yet receipted at destination.

Transactional record of physical inventory cycle count events conducted at storage locations. Captures count date, count method (full physical, ABC cycle, perpetual), counted quantity, system quantity, variance quantity, variance percentage, count status (planned, in-progress, confirmed, posted), and approver. Supports inventory accuracy KPIs, shrinkage investigation triggers, and WMS reconciliation. Distinct from stock_movement as it represents a formal audit event, not a stock transaction.
affected_objects.after: Cycle count activities for inventory accuracy

affected_objects.before: Transactional record of inventory replenishment requests and orders generated through VMI auto-replenishment, distribution requirements planning (DRP), or manual triggers. Captures replenishment type, requested quantity, approved quantity, source location, destination location, requested delivery date, priority, and fulfillment status. Closes the loop between demand sensing signals and physical stock movement execution.

Master record for physical and logical storage locations within the distribution network including distribution centers, warehouses, retail back-rooms, 3PL facilities, and in-transit staging areas. Captures location code, location type (bulk, pick, reserve, quarantine, returns), temperature zone, capacity (weight, volume, pallet positions), WMS zone mapping, and geo-coordinates. Serves as the single source of truth for the location hierarchy used across warehouse management and inventory systems.

Master record defining Vendor Managed Inventory (VMI) agreements between Consumer Goods and its retail/distributor customers. Captures VMI partner (retailer/distributor), covered SKUs, min/max stock levels at partner location, replenishment frequency, data sharing method (EDI, TradeEdge), service level commitment, VMI start date, VMI end date, and agreement status. Distinct from replenishment_order (the execution) — this is the governing policy for VMI-managed inventory relationships.

Master record for each manufactured or received lot/batch of a SKU, capturing batch number, manufacturing date, expiry date, best-before date, country of origin, GMP status, and quarantine flags. Supports FEFO/FIFO rotation enforcement, lot-level traceability for recall readiness, and regulatory compliance (FDA 21 CFR Part 11, EU REACH, EU Food Information Regulation). Linked to production batch records in manufacturing execution systems and quality inspection lots.
affected_objects.after: Lot and batch tracking for inventory traceability

affected_objects.before: Transactional record capturing Out-of-Stock (OOS) and On-Shelf Availability (OSA) events at the SKU-location level. Captures OOS start timestamp, OOS end timestamp, OOS duration (hours), root cause category (demand spike, replenishment failure, forecast miss, upstream stockout, logistics delay), estimated lost sales value, and resolution action. Sourced from POS data feeds and demand sensing signals. Critical for OSA improvement programs, retail execution accountability, and service level reporting.

Master record for product recall and withdrawal events triggered by safety, quality, or regulatory findings. Captures recall classification (Class I/II/III FDA, voluntary withdrawal), affected SKUs, affected lot/batch ranges, recall scope (geographic, channel, customer), recall initiation date, regulatory notification date (FDA/CPSC), quantity recalled, quantity recovered, recall status, and financial impact estimate. Supports lot_batch traceability queries and regulatory reporting obligations.
affected_objects.after: Product recall events and affected inventory

affected_objects.before: Transactional record of inventory reservations that earmark specific stock quantities for confirmed sales orders, production orders, promotional commitments, or intercompany transfers. Captures reservation type (sales order, production, promotional, intercompany), reserved quantity, reserved lot/batch (if FEFO-specific), reservation date, expiry date of reservation, fulfillment status, and consuming document reference. Prevents double-allocation of available stock across competing demand streams.
affected_objects.after: Inventory reservations for orders and allocations

affected_objects.before: Master record defining safety stock parameters and reorder point policies for each SKU-location combination. Captures safety stock quantity, reorder point, maximum stock level, minimum order quantity (MOQ), replenishment lead time, service level target (%), demand variability coefficient, and policy review date. Feeds SAP IBP inventory optimization and DRP planning runs. Distinct from stock_position (actual balance) — this is the policy/rule that governs when replenishment is triggered.
affected_objects.after: Safety stock policies by SKU and location

affected_objects.before: Transactional record of manual and system-generated inventory adjustments that correct stock balances outside of normal goods movement flows. Captures adjustment reason (shrinkage, damage, system reconciliation, theft, sampling, promotional giveaway), adjusted quantity, adjusted value, adjustment date, approver, and supporting reference document. Distinct from stock_movement (which covers standard GR/GI flows) — adjustments represent exception corrections to the inventory ledger.

Transactional record of quality holds, regulatory blocks, and commercial holds placed on inventory lots or stock positions. Captures hold type (QC inspection hold, regulatory recall hold, commercial dispute hold, damage hold), hold reason, hold quantity, hold start date, hold release date, hold status, approving authority, and disposition decision (release, rework, destroy, return to supplier). Integrates with quality management usage decisions and regulatory hold workflows.
affected_objects.after: Inventory holds for quality or regulatory reasons

affected_objects.before: Transactional record of every inventory movement event including goods receipts, goods issues, stock transfers, returns, write-offs, and inter-plant transfers. Captures movement type code, quantity, unit of measure, source and destination locations, posting date, reference document (purchase order, production order, delivery note), carrier/shipment reference for inter-node transfers, and posting user. Provides the full audit trail for inventory reconciliation and in-transit tracking.

Core master record of physical inventory on-hand quantities for each SKU at each storage location. Captures unrestricted, quality-hold, blocked, consignment, VMI-managed, and in-transit stock quantities by stock type and special stock indicator. Serves as the authoritative real-time inventory balance (single source of truth for quantity on hand). Supports OOS/OSA monitoring, days-inventory-outstanding calculation, available-to-promise derivation, and multi-echelon inventory visibility across the distribution network.
affected_objects.after: Current inventory position by SKU, location, and lot/batch

affected_objects.before: Transactional record of inventory valuation snapshots for each SKU-location combination, capturing standard cost, moving average price, total stock value, COGS allocation, inventory write-down amounts, and valuation method (standard cost, FIFO, weighted average). Aligned with material ledger postings in the financial system. Supports COGS reporting, days-inventory-outstanding calculation, and financial close processes. Distinct from stock_position (quantity) — this captures the monetary value dimension of inventory.
Master reference table for warehouse. Referenced by warehouse_id.

before.description: Actual date and time when the shipment physically arrived at the destination node. Null until arrival occurs. Used for OTIF performance measurement.
Production batch identifier for granular traceability within a lot. Used for quality assurance and regulatory compliance.
Identifier of the logistics carrier or third-party logistics provider (3PL) responsible for transporting the shipment.
The transportation service level or speed tier selected for this shipment, impacting transit time and cost.
Actual date and time when the shipment physically departed from the origin node. Used for transit time calculation and OTIF (On Time In Full) measurement.
Identifier of the target location in the distribution network where the shipment is being delivered (distribution center, warehouse, retail store, or customer location).
Classification of the destination location type in the supply chain network.
Detailed narrative description of the exception event, including root cause and resolution actions taken.
Boolean indicator of whether the shipment encountered any exceptions during transit (delays, damage, routing issues, temperature excursions).
Classification of the primary exception encountered during shipment transit. Null if no exception occurred.
Total freight transportation cost for this shipment in the base currency. Used for logistics cost allocation and freight audit.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the freight cost amount.
DOT hazard class code for hazardous materials (e.g., 3 for flammable liquids, 8 for corrosives). Null if not hazmat.
Boolean indicator of whether the shipment contains hazardous materials requiring special handling, labeling, and regulatory compliance.
Boolean indicator of whether the shipment arrived with the complete expected quantity, regardless of timing.
Total quantity of inventory units currently in-transit for this shipment. Represents stock that has left origin but not yet arrived at destination.
Date and time when this in-transit shipment record was most recently modified. Used for change tracking and data freshness monitoring.
Manufacturing lot or batch number for traceability and recall readiness. Critical for FEFO (First Expired First Out) rotation and quality control.
Boolean indicator of whether the shipment arrived on or before the expected arrival date, regardless of quantity accuracy.
Foreign key linking to sales.order. Business justification: Required for shipment‑to‑order tracking in OTIF logistics reports; sales order is the business driver for each in‑transit shipment.
Classification of the origin location type in the supply chain network.
Boolean indicator of whether the shipment met OTIF performance criteria (arrived on time with full quantity). True if both time and quantity targets were met.
Number of pallets included in this shipment. Used for warehouse receiving planning and dock scheduling.
Identifier of the source location in the distribution network from which the shipment departed (supplier facility, distribution center, warehouse, or manufacturing plant).
Purchase order number associated with this shipment, linking the in-transit inventory to the originating procurement transaction.
Unit of measure for the in-transit quantity (each, case, pallet, weight, volume). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: each|case|pallet|kg|lbs|liter|gallon — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

Date and time when the shipment was formally receipted into destination inventory through WMS (Warehouse Management System). May differ from arrival timestamp due to inspection and put-away processes.
Maximum acceptable temperature in Celsius for temperature-controlled shipments. Used for cold chain compliance monitoring.
Minimum acceptable temperature in Celsius for temperature-controlled shipments. Used for cold chain compliance monitoring.

Foreign key linking to research.research_formulation. Business justification: Launch logistics report tracks shipments of newly launched formulations, tying in‑transit data to the formulation for rollout monitoring.
External business identifier for the shipment, used for tracking and communication with carriers and logistics partners. May be ASN (Advanced Shipping Notice) number or BOL (Bill of Lading) number.
Total volume of the shipment in cubic meters. Used for transportation capacity planning and dimensional weight calculations.
Total gross weight of the shipment in kilograms, including packaging. Used for freight cost calculation and carrier capacity planning.
Boolean indicator of whether this shipment requires temperature-controlled transportation (cold chain logistics) to maintain product quality and safety.
Number of calendar days the shipment was in transit from departure to arrival. Calculated as the difference between actual arrival and departure timestamps.
Primary mode of transportation used for moving the shipment between origin and destination.
The ABC inventory classification of the SKU at the time of count. A = high-value items counted frequently, B = medium-value, C = low-value counted less frequently. Drives cycle count frequency.
The ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) document number or transaction ID generated when the inventory adjustment was posted. Used for financial audit trail and reconciliation.
Indicates whether the variance has been posted as an inventory adjustment in the ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) system. True = adjustment posted, False = pending posting.
Date and time when the cycle count was approved by the authorized supervisor. Part of the audit trail for inventory adjustments.
Identifier of the supervisor or manager who approved the cycle count results and authorized the variance adjustment. Required for SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) compliance and segregation of duties.

The methodology used for the cycle count. Full physical = complete inventory audit, ABC cycle = frequency-based counting by value classification, perpetual = continuous counting, spot check = random verification, blind count = counter does not see system quantity.
The warehouse zone or area designation where the count took place (e.g., receiving, picking, reserve, quarantine). Used for zone-based cycle count scheduling.
The expiration or best-before date of the lot/batch counted. Critical for FEFO (First Expired First Out) rotation rules and consumer safety in CPG (Consumer Packaged Goods).
The total monetary value of the counted inventory based on the counted quantity and the unit cost at the time of count. Used for financial reconciliation and shrinkage cost calculation.
Date and time when the cycle count record was last updated. Tracks changes through the count lifecycle (planned → in_progress → confirmed → posted).
Manufacturing lot or batch number of the inventory counted. Critical for traceability and recall readiness in consumer goods.
Identifier of the warehouse or distribution center where the cycle count was performed. Supports multi-site inventory management.
If this is a recount, references the inventory_cycle_count_id of the original count that triggered the recount requirement. Null for initial counts.
Identifier of the warehouse associate or employee who performed the physical count. Used for accountability and performance tracking.
Indicates whether the counted inventory is in quarantine status pending quality inspection or regulatory clearance. True = quarantined, False = available.
Indicates whether this cycle count is a recount of a previous count that exceeded variance thresholds. True = recount, False = initial count.
Indicates whether the counted inventory is stored in a temperature-controlled environment. True = cold chain storage, False = ambient. Relevant for perishable consumer goods.
Free-text explanation or additional context provided by the counter or approver regarding the variance. Used for investigation and documentation.

Categorization of the root cause for the inventory variance. Used for shrinkage analysis, process improvement, and loss prevention. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: shrinkage|damage|misplacement|system_error|receiving_error|picking_error|expiration|theft|administrative_error|vendor_shortage — promote to reference product]

The monetary value of the variance (variance_quantity * unit_cost). Represents the financial impact of the inventory discrepancy. Used for shrinkage reporting and P&L (Profit and Loss) impact analysis.
Actual date the shipment was received at the destination location. Used to measure delivery performance and OTIF compliance.
Actual date the shipment departed from the source location. Used to calculate On Time In Full (OTIF) performance.
Quantity of the SKU approved for fulfillment after review and Available to Promise (ATP) validation. May differ from requested quantity due to supply constraints.

Foreign key linking to marketing.campaign. Business justification: Promotional campaigns trigger dedicated replenishment orders; linking enables the Campaign‑Driven Replenishment Report used in trade spend planning.
Explanation for why the replenishment order was cancelled, if applicable. Examples include demand change, supply constraint, or duplicate order.
Reference to the logistics carrier assigned to transport this replenishment shipment from source to destination.
Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Replenishment orders are charged to cost centers for budgeting and cost tracking of inventory replenishment.
Identifier of the warehouse, distribution center, or retail location that will receive the replenished inventory.
Date after which the product should not be sold or used. Used to enforce First Expired First Out (FEFO) rotation rules in inventory management.
Total freight cost incurred for transporting this replenishment order from source to destination location.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the freight cost amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).
Date and time when the replenishment order record was last updated in the system.
Expected number of days between order placement and delivery at the destination location, based on historical lane performance.
Manufacturing lot or batch number assigned to the inventory being replenished. Critical for traceability and recall readiness per Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) requirements.
Indicates whether this replenishment order was created to prevent an anticipated Out of Stock (OOS) event based on demand forecasting.
Date and time when the replenishment order was approved for fulfillment by the supply chain planner or automated approval workflow.
Date and time when the replenishment order was cancelled, if applicable. Null for active orders.
Date and time when the replenishment order was first created in the system, either automatically by planning algorithms or manually by a planner.
Free-text field for planners to capture special instructions, handling requirements, or contextual information about the replenishment order.
Identifier of the system user or automated process that created the replenishment order.
Identifier of the warehouse, distribution center, or manufacturing facility from which inventory will be shipped to fulfill this replenishment order.
Business priority assigned to the replenishment order to guide fulfillment sequencing and resource allocation. Critical orders address Out of Stock (OOS) situations.
Foreign key linking to finance.profit_center. Business justification: Profit‑center allocation of replenishment orders supports segment‑level expense reporting.
Foreign key linking to procurement.purchase_requisition. Business justification: REQUIRED: Internal replenishment orders are driven by purchase requisitions; linking supports demand‑driven planning.
Actual quantity received and confirmed at the destination location. May differ from shipped quantity due to damage or discrepancies.
Business-facing unique identifier for the replenishment order, used for tracking and communication across systems and stakeholders.
Quantity of the SKU requested for replenishment, as calculated by the demand planning system or entered by the planner.
Inventory rotation policy applied to this replenishment: First Expired First Out (FEFO) for perishables, First In First Out (FIFO) for standard goods, Last In First Out (LIFO) for specific scenarios.
Indicates whether this replenishment order was triggered by inventory falling below the safety stock threshold at the destination location.
Planned date for shipment departure from the source location, calculated based on lead time and requested delivery date.
Carrier-provided tracking number for the shipment associated with this replenishment order. Used for in-transit visibility.
Actual quantity shipped from the source location. Updated when the shipment is dispatched.
ABC analysis classification for the location based on inventory velocity and value. A for high-velocity/high-value, B for medium, C for low-velocity/low-value items. Used for slotting optimization.
Date when the location was blocked or made unavailable for inventory placement.
Explanation for why the location is blocked or unavailable, used for operational troubleshooting and compliance documentation.
Number of standard pallet positions that can be stored in this location, used for pallet-based inventory planning.
Maximum volumetric capacity of the storage location in cubic meters, used for space utilization optimization.
Indicates whether this location is designated for cross-docking operations where goods move directly from receiving to shipping without long-term storage.
Date when the storage location was decommissioned or removed from active use. Null for currently active locations.
Date when the storage location became operational and available for inventory placement.
Indicates whether the storage location is certified and equipped for storing hazardous materials per regulatory requirements.

Foreign key linking to regulatory.jurisdiction. Business justification: Regulatory reporting requires mapping each storage location to its jurisdiction for local compliance (labeling, safety, reporting).
Date of the most recent physical inventory count or cycle count performed at this location, used for inventory accuracy tracking.
Timestamp when this storage location record was most recently updated for change tracking and audit compliance.
Timestamp of the most recent inventory movement (putaway, pick, transfer) at this location, used for activity analysis and slotting optimization.
Geographic latitude coordinate of the storage location for geospatial analytics, route optimization, and facility mapping.
Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Each storage location has a manager responsible for inventory integrity; used in location performance and accountability reports.
Geographic longitude coordinate of the storage location for geospatial analytics, route optimization, and facility mapping.
Reference to the parent facility (distribution center, warehouse, retail store, or third-party logistics provider) where this storage location resides.
Indicates whether the location permits storage of multiple SKUs simultaneously or requires single-SKU dedication for inventory accuracy.

Foreign key linking to supply.network_node. Business justification: WAREHOUSE MANAGEMENT: each storage location is physically part of a supply network node; required for location‑level inventory reporting.
Numeric priority ranking for order picking optimization. Lower numbers indicate higher priority for fast-moving SKUs and efficient pick path planning.
Percentage threshold that triggers automatic replenishment from reserve to pick locations. Used in Vendor Managed Inventory (VMI) and automated replenishment processes.

Inventory rotation policy applied to this location. FEFO (First Expired First Out) for perishables, FIFO (First In First Out) for standard goods, LIFO (Last In First Out) for specific scenarios, or MANUAL for operator-controlled picking.

Security classification of the storage location based on access controls and monitoring requirements. High-value for premium products, controlled substance for regulated materials, restricted for limited access areas.

Temperature control classification for the storage location. Ambient for room temperature, refrigerated for 2-8°C, frozen for below 0°C, and controlled for specific temperature ranges required by product specifications.
Reference to the third-party logistics provider managing this location, if applicable. Null for company-owned facilities.
WMS zone identifier used for warehouse layout management, picking optimization, and labor allocation. Zones group locations by operational characteristics or product categories.
Indicates whether automated replenishment orders are triggered based on inventory levels without manual approval.
Frequency at which invoices are generated for inventory replenished under this VMI agreement.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for financial transactions under this VMI agreement.
Technical method or platform used to exchange inventory visibility and replenishment data between Consumer Goods and the VMI partner.
Specific EDI transaction set codes used for VMI data exchange (e.g., 846 Inventory Inquiry/Advice, 852 Product Activity Data).
Date when the VMI agreement expires or terminates. Nullable for open-ended agreements.
Date when the VMI agreement becomes active and binding.
Indicates whether demand forecast data is shared between Consumer Goods and the VMI partner for collaborative planning.
Defines who owns the inventory at the partner location until point of sale or consumption.
Current lifecycle status of the VMI agreement.
Timestamp when this VMI agreement record was last updated.
Indicates whether lot or batch traceability is mandatory for inventory managed under this VMI agreement for recall readiness.
Maximum inventory quantity threshold at partner location to avoid overstocking.
Minimum inventory quantity threshold at partner location that triggers replenishment.
Free-text field for additional comments, special terms, or operational notes related to the VMI agreement.
Description of financial or operational penalties applied if out-of-stock events occur at partner location.
Target percentage for deliveries that meet both on-time and in-full criteria as defined in the VMI agreement.
Indicates whether point-of-sale transaction data is shared by the partner to enable demand sensing and replenishment optimization.
Email address of the primary business contact at the VMI partner for operational communication.
Name of the primary business contact at the VMI partner responsible for this agreement.
Phone number of the primary business contact at the VMI partner for urgent escalations.
Identifier of the Consumer Goods employee responsible for managing this VMI agreement.
Number of days prior to expiration that renewal notice must be provided to continue the VMI agreement.
Number of days required from replenishment trigger to delivery at partner location.
Identifier of the specific partner warehouse, distribution center, or retail location covered by this VMI agreement.
Inventory rotation policy applied at partner location (FEFO = First Expired First Out, FIFO = First In First Out).
Buffer inventory quantity maintained to mitigate stockout risk due to demand variability or supply disruption.
Committed service level percentage for on-time in-full (OTIF) delivery under this VMI agreement.
Unit of measure for all stock level thresholds (e.g., cases, pallets, eaches, kilograms).
Optimal inventory quantity to maintain at partner location under normal conditions.
Number of days advance notice required to terminate the VMI agreement by either party.
Identifier of the user who last modified this VMI agreement record.
The current lifecycle status of the lot or batch. Indicates whether the batch is active and available, depleted, expired, recalled, destroyed, or transferred to another location.
The unique identifier for the Certificate of Analysis document that records the quality test results for this lot or batch.
Free-text notes documenting regulatory compliance status, exceptions, or special handling requirements for this lot or batch.
The username or identifier of the user who created this lot or batch record. Used for audit trail and accountability.
Foreign key linking to regulatory.dossier. Business justification: Batch traceability links each lot/batch to its regulatory dossier for post‑market surveillance and recall investigations.
Indicates whether this lot or batch was produced in compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice standards. Critical for regulatory compliance and quality assurance.
Boolean flag indicating whether this lot or batch is on hold and cannot be used or shipped. True if on hold, False otherwise.
The business reason why this lot or batch is on hold, if applicable. Examples: pending quality review, regulatory investigation, customer complaint.
The date on which quality control inspection was performed on this lot or batch.

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Regulatory quality inspection requires recording the employee ID of the inspector for each batch; essential for traceability and compliance audits.
The date on which this lot or batch was manufactured or produced. Critical for shelf-life calculation and First Expired First Out (FEFO) rotation.

Foreign key linking to marketing.brand. Business justification: Brand‑level lot traceability is required for quality compliance and consumer‑facing brand claims; linking lot_batch to brand supports this.
The username or identifier of the user who last modified this lot or batch record. Used for audit trail and accountability.
The timestamp when this lot or batch record was last modified in the system. Used for audit trail and change tracking.
Free-text notes or comments about this lot or batch. May include special handling instructions, quality observations, or other relevant information.
The production order or work order number under which this lot or batch was manufactured. Links to Manufacturing Execution System (MES) records.

The quality grade or classification assigned to this lot or batch based on quality control inspection results. May affect pricing, distribution channel, or disposal decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: A|B|C|premium|standard|substandard|rejected — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
The total quantity of product manufactured in this lot or batch, measured in the base unit of measure.
Current quarantine or release status of the lot or batch. Quarantined lots cannot be used or shipped until quality inspection is complete and status is changed to released.
The date on which this lot or batch was received into inventory, applicable for purchased or transferred goods.
Boolean flag indicating whether this lot or batch meets all applicable regulatory compliance requirements. True if compliant, False otherwise.
The number of days remaining until expiry_date as of the current date. Used for inventory rotation and markdown decisions.

Foreign key linking to research.research_formulation. Business justification: Regulatory compliance mandates batch‑to‑formulation mapping to verify that each produced lot follows the approved formulation.
The number of days from manufacturing_date to expiry_date, representing the total shelf life of this lot or batch. Used for First Expired First Out (FEFO) calculations.
The required storage conditions for this lot or batch to maintain product quality and safety. Examples: ambient, refrigerated, frozen, controlled room temperature.
The warehouse or storage location code where this lot or batch is currently stored. Used for inventory visibility and warehouse management.
The lot or batch number assigned by the supplier for received raw materials or finished goods. Used for traceability back to the supplier in case of quality issues or recalls.
A unique code used for end-to-end supply chain traceability of this lot or batch. May be a GS1 Global Trade Item Number (GTIN) with batch extension or similar standard.

The unit in which quantity_produced is measured. Examples: EA (each), CS (case), KG (kilogram), L (liter). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|CS|KG|LB|L|GAL|M|FT — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
The name of the vendor or supplier from whom this lot or batch was received, if applicable for purchased goods.
Actual observed demand in units during the OOS event period, used to identify demand spikes or forecast misses.
Brand name of the SKU that experienced the OOS event, used for brand-level OOS performance tracking.
Distribution channel type where the OOS event occurred: retail, wholesale, e-commerce, DSD (Direct Store Delivery), or DTC (Direct to Consumer).
Description of the corrective action plan implemented to prevent recurrence of similar OOS events in the future.
Boolean flag indicating whether the OOS event resulted in direct customer impact such as lost sales, customer complaints, or service level breaches.
Forecasted demand in units for the period during which the OOS event occurred, used to compare actual vs. planned demand.
System or channel that detected and reported the out-of-stock event, such as POS system, WMS, demand sensing platform, manual report, retail execution app, or EDI feed.
Estimated monetary value of sales lost due to the out-of-stock condition, calculated based on historical demand patterns and average selling price.
Estimated quantity of units that could not be sold due to the out-of-stock condition.
Current lifecycle status of the OOS event record: open (active OOS), resolved (inventory restored), under investigation (root cause analysis in progress), or closed (fully resolved and documented).
Forecast accuracy percentage for the SKU-location during the period of the OOS event, calculated as (1 - |actual - forecast| / actual) * 100.
Severity classification of the OOS event impact based on lost sales value, SKU importance, and customer impact. Categories: critical, high, medium, low.
System-recorded inventory quantity on hand at the time the OOS event was detected, used to identify phantom inventory situations.
Date of the most recent replenishment delivery prior to the OOS event, used to analyze replenishment frequency adequacy.
Timestamp when the OOS event record was most recently updated, reflecting changes to status, resolution actions, or root cause analysis.
Date of the next scheduled replenishment delivery at the time of the OOS event, used to assess replenishment planning gaps.

Classification of the OOS event type: warehouse stockout (no inventory in facility), shelf stockout (inventory in back room but not on shelf), phantom inventory (system shows stock but physical count is zero), or system mismatch.
Actual on-shelf availability percentage achieved during the period including the OOS event, calculated from POS and inventory data.
Target on-shelf availability percentage for the SKU-location at the time of the OOS event, used to measure performance against goals.
Reference to the previous OOS event ID for the same SKU-location if this is a recurrence, enabling trend analysis.
Product category classification of the SKU that experienced the OOS event, used for category-level OOS analysis and reporting.
Boolean flag indicating whether this OOS event is a recurrence of a previous OOS event for the same SKU-location combination within a defined time window.
Configured reorder point threshold for the SKU at this location, used to evaluate whether replenishment triggers were properly set.
Timestamp when the resolution action was initiated or completed to address the out-of-stock condition.

Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Out‑of‑stock events are owned by a specific employee who drives corrective actions; required for OOS root‑cause analysis and SLA reporting.
Primary root cause classification for the OOS event. Categories include demand spike, replenishment failure, forecast miss, upstream stockout, logistics delay, or system error.
Detailed narrative explanation of the root cause behind the out-of-stock event, providing context beyond the category classification.
Configured safety stock level for the SKU at this location at the time of the OOS event, used to assess whether safety stock was breached.
Boolean flag indicating whether the OOS event caused a breach of service level agreement commitments to customers or retail partners.
Comma-separated list of GTIN/UPC/EAN codes for recalled products. Enables point-of-sale blocking and supply chain traceability across trading partners using GS1 standards.
Specification of the lot numbers, batch codes, or serial number ranges included in the recall. Critical for traceability and targeted recovery. May be expressed as ranges, lists, or patterns.
Comprehensive description of the product(s) subject to recall, including brand names, product names, sizes, formulations, and any distinguishing characteristics. Used for consumer identification.
Comma-separated or structured list of SKU codes for all products included in the recall scope. Links to product master for detailed SKU attributes and enables inventory queries.
Date when the regulatory authority officially closed the recall after reviewing effectiveness checks and final reports. Nullable until regulatory closure is granted.
Date when all recall activities were completed, including product recovery, customer notification, and corrective actions. Nullable until recall is finished.

Primary method(s) used to notify consumers about the recall. Press Release: public media announcement. Direct Mail: letters to registered consumers. Email: electronic notification. Phone: direct phone contact. Social Media: notification via social platforms. Retail Signage: point-of-sale notices. Multiple Methods: combination approach. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Press Release|Direct Mail|Email|Phone|Social Media|Retail Signage|Multiple Methods — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

Description of corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) implemented to address the root cause and prevent recurrence. Includes process changes, equipment modifications, supplier changes, and quality system improvements.

Level in the distribution chain to which the recall extends. Consumer Level: recall reaches end consumers. Retail Level: recall stops at retail stores. Wholesale Level: recall stops at wholesalers/distributors. Distribution Center: recall stops at company distribution centers before reaching trade.

Estimated total financial impact of the recall including product cost, logistics, customer credits, disposal, regulatory fines, and brand impact. Expressed in reporting currency. Used for financial reserves and management reporting.
Latest expiration or best-by date printed on recalled products. Defines the full date range for consumer identification.
Earliest expiration or best-by date printed on recalled products. Helps consumers and retailers identify affected units on shelf.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the estimated financial impact amount. Enables multi-currency recall cost tracking and consolidation.
FDA or internal assessment of the health risk posed by the recalled product. Describes potential adverse health consequences and likelihood of occurrence. Used to determine recall classification.
Date when the recall was officially initiated by the company. This is the business event date when the decision to recall was made and communicated internally.

The unit in which the inventory was counted. EA = each, CS = case, PL = pallet, KG = kilogram, LB = pound, L = liter, GAL = gallon. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|CS|PL|KG|LB|L|GAL — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
The variance expressed as a percentage of the system quantity. Calculated as (variance_quantity / system_quantity) * 100. Used to trigger investigation thresholds.
The difference between counted quantity and system quantity (counted minus system). Positive values indicate overage, negative values indicate shortage.
Unique identifier for the inventory replenishment order record. Primary key for this entity.

Current lifecycle status of the replenishment order indicating its position in the fulfillment workflow. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|submitted|approved|rejected|in_transit|received|cancelled — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

Classification of the replenishment order generation method: Vendor Managed Inventory (VMI) auto-replenishment, Distribution Requirements Planning (DRP) planned order, manual trigger by planner, safety stock replenishment, emergency order, or seasonal build.
Target date by which the replenishment inventory is needed at the destination location to prevent Out of Stock (OOS) conditions.
Reference to the specific SKU being replenished. Links to the product master for item details.

Standard unit in which the replenishment quantity is expressed: Each (EA), Case (CS), Pallet (PL), Pound (LB), Kilogram (KG), Liter (L), Gallon (GAL). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|CS|PL|LB|KG|L|GAL — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Aisle designation within the warehouse layout for physical navigation and location addressing.
Bay or section identifier within an aisle, representing a vertical or horizontal subdivision of storage space.
Bin or slot identifier representing the smallest addressable storage unit within a level, used for item-level location precision.
Maximum weight capacity of the storage location in kilograms, used for load planning and safety compliance.
Timestamp when this storage location record was first created in the system for audit trail and data lineage.
Unique identifier for the storage location within the distribution network. Primary key.
Vertical level or shelf position within a bay, used for precise location addressing in multi-tier racking systems.
Business identifier for the storage location used across warehouse management and inventory systems. Unique alphanumeric code assigned to each physical or logical storage position.
Human-readable name or description of the storage location for operational reference and reporting.

Current operational status of the storage location. Active for normal operations, blocked for temporary holds, maintenance for repairs, quarantine for quality issues, inactive for unused space, decommissioned for permanently retired locations.

Classification of the storage location based on its operational purpose within the warehouse. Bulk storage for palletized goods, pick locations for order fulfillment, reserve for overflow, quarantine for quality hold, returns for reverse logistics, and staging for in-transit goods.
Descriptive name or title of the VMI agreement for business reference.
Business-facing unique identifier or contract number for the VMI agreement.
Classification of the VMI agreement based on scope and strategic importance.
Timestamp when this VMI agreement record was first created in the system.
Unique identifier for the VMI agreement record. Primary key.
Agreed payment terms for invoices related to VMI replenishment (e.g., Net 30, Net 60, 2/10 Net 30).
Scheduled frequency at which inventory replenishment occurs under this VMI agreement.
Identifier of the retail or distributor partner participating in the VMI arrangement.
The externally-known unique batch or lot number assigned during manufacturing. Used for traceability and recall management.
The date until which the product retains optimal quality. Distinct from expiry_date; product may still be safe but quality may degrade after this date.
The three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code representing the country where this lot or batch was manufactured. Required for customs, trade compliance, and labeling.
The timestamp when this lot or batch record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.
The date after which the product should not be used or sold. Used to enforce First Expired First Out (FEFO) inventory rotation and prevent sale of expired goods.
Unique identifier for the lot or batch record. Primary key for the lot_batch product.
Alternative or supplementary lot identifier used in some manufacturing contexts. May be the same as batch_number or represent a sub-batch.
Reference to the manufacturing facility where this lot or batch was produced.
The date by which the lot or batch must be retested to confirm continued quality and compliance. Common in pharmaceutical and chemical manufacturing.
Reference to the SKU that this lot or batch represents. Links to the product master.
Timestamp when the OOS event record was first created in the system.
Identifier of the warehouse, distribution center, or retail location where the OOS event occurred.
Total duration of the out-of-stock event measured in hours, calculated as the difference between end and start timestamps.
Timestamp when the out-of-stock condition was resolved and inventory became available again.
Unique identifier for the out-of-stock event record.
Timestamp when the out-of-stock condition was first detected. Sourced from POS data feeds or demand sensing signals.
Action taken to resolve the out-of-stock event, such as emergency replenishment, transfer from alternate location, expedited shipment, customer backorder, substitution offered, or no action taken.
Identifier of the SKU that experienced the out-of-stock condition.
Timestamp when this recall event record was first created in the system. Audit trail for data lineage and compliance reporting.
Foreign key linking to regulatory.product_recall. Business justification: Internal recall events must be tied to the external regulatory product recall record to align actions and reporting.
Actual quantity of recalled product recovered from the market through returns, destructions, and corrections. Updated throughout recall lifecycle. Used to calculate recall effectiveness percentage.
Unique identifier for the product recall or withdrawal event. Primary key.
External recall identification number assigned by the company or regulatory authority for tracking and communication purposes.

Current lifecycle status of the recall event. Initiated: recall has been declared and communication started. In Progress: active recovery and customer notification underway. Ongoing: recall activities continuing. Completed: all recall activities finished, awaiting final regulatory closure. Terminated: recall ended by firm decision. Closed: regulatory authority has reviewed and closed the recall.

Primary reason category for the recall event. Safety: product poses health or safety risk. Quality: product fails quality specifications. Regulatory: non-compliance with regulations. Labeling: incorrect or missing label information. Contamination: presence of foreign material or microbial contamination. Allergen: undeclared allergen present.

Primary regulatory authority overseeing this recall. FDA: U.S. Food and Drug Administration. CPSC: Consumer Product Safety Commission. EPA: Environmental Protection Agency. EU REACH: European chemicals regulation. Health Canada: Canadian health authority. ANVISA: Brazilian health authority. TGA: Australian Therapeutic Goods Administration. MHRA: UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: FDA|CPSC|EPA|EU REACH|Health Canada|ANVISA|TGA|MHRA|Other — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Date and time when the reservation record was first created in the system.
Date after which the reservation automatically expires if not fulfilled, releasing the reserved stock back to available inventory.
Reference to the warehouse storage location where the reserved inventory is physically held.
Date when the inventory reservation was created and stock was earmarked for this demand.
Business-facing unique reservation number used for tracking and reference across systems and documents.
Current lifecycle status of the reservation indicating whether it is active, partially fulfilled, fully fulfilled, cancelled, or expired.
Classification of the reservation purpose: sales order fulfillment, production consumption, promotional commitment, intercompany transfer, quality hold, or safety stock allocation.
Quantity of inventory units reserved and earmarked for this specific demand. Measured in the product's base unit of measure.
Reference to the specific product or Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) for which inventory is reserved.
Standard unit of measure for the reserved quantity (e.g., EA for each, CS for case, KG for kilogram).
The date and time when this safety stock policy record was first created in the system.
The upper inventory threshold for this SKU-location combination. Prevents overstocking and excess inventory carrying costs.

Classification of the safety stock policy methodology. Fixed policies use static parameters; dynamic policies adjust based on demand variability; seasonal policies account for cyclical patterns; promotional policies support campaign-driven demand; VMI (Vendor Managed Inventory) policies are supplier-controlled; consignment policies apply to stock owned by suppliers.
The inventory level at which a replenishment order should be triggered. Calculated as safety stock plus demand during lead time.
Unique identifier for the safety stock policy record. Primary key.

The target safety stock quantity to be maintained at the location for this SKU, expressed in the base unit of measure. This buffer inventory protects against demand variability and supply uncertainty.
Reference to the product SKU governed by this safety stock policy.
The base unit in which safety stock quantities are expressed (e.g., EA for each, CS for case, PL for pallet).
Business date when the inventory adjustment was physically identified or when the correction event occurred, distinct from system posting date.
Precise date and time when the adjustment transaction was created or recorded in the system.
Classification of the adjustment transaction indicating the nature of the inventory correction (physical count variance, shrinkage, damage, expiry, system reconciliation, theft).
System timestamp when the adjustment record was first created in the database, used for audit trail and data lineage.
Three-letter ISO currency code for the adjusted value and unit cost (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).
Free-text field for additional comments, observations, or contextual information about the adjustment that may be relevant for audit or operational review.
Identifier of the product or Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) being adjusted.
Standard or moving average cost per unit of the inventory item at the time of adjustment, used for inventory valuation.
Unit of measure for the adjusted quantity (e.g., EA for each, CS for case, KG for kilogram, LT for liter).
Identifier of the warehouse or distribution center where the inventory adjustment occurred.
Timestamp when this hold record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage.
Date when the hold was placed on the inventory. This is the business event date when the stock became restricted.
Current lifecycle status of the hold. Active holds block inventory movement; released holds allow disposition; pending review awaits approval; escalated holds require management intervention.
Classification of the hold reason. Quality Control (QC) inspection hold, regulatory recall hold, commercial dispute hold, damage hold, quarantine hold, or investigation hold.
Identifier of the warehouse or distribution center where the held inventory is located.
Timestamp when this stock movement record was first created in the system for audit trail.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the movement value (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).
System user ID of the person who posted or recorded this stock movement for audit trail and accountability.
Precise date and time when the physical inventory movement occurred or was recorded in the system.
Quantity of inventory moved in this transaction. Positive for receipts/increases, negative for issues/decreases.
Document number of the source transaction (PO number, production order number, delivery note number) that triggered this movement.

Type of source document that initiated this stock movement for audit trail and reconciliation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: purchase_order|production_order|sales_order|delivery_note|transfer_order|return_order|adjustment_document — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Reference to the SKU involved in this stock movement event.
Unique identifier for the stock movement transaction. Primary key for the stock movement record.
Unit of measure for the movement quantity (e.g., EA=Each, CS=Case, KG=Kilogram, LT=Liter).
Timestamp when the stock position record was first created in the system.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the inventory valuation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: USD|EUR|GBP|JPY|CNY|CAD|AUD|INR|BRL|MXN — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Quantity of stock currently in transit between locations (plant-to-warehouse, warehouse-to-store, etc.) and not yet received at destination.
Reference to the physical storage location (warehouse, distribution center, store, or specific bin) where the inventory is held.

Foreign key linking to inventory.lot_batch. Business justification: Batch‑level inventory reconciliation report requires linking each stock position to its lot_batch for traceability of production dates and quality attributes.
Quantity of stock reserved for specific sales orders, production orders, or other commitments and not available for general allocation.
Reference to the specific SKU for which inventory is held. Links to the product master data.
Unique identifier for the stock position record. Primary key for the stock position entity.

Current lifecycle status of the stock position. Active=available for operations; Inactive=temporarily unavailable; Pending Disposal=marked for write-off; Transferred=moved to another location; Consumed=used in production or sold.

Unit in which the quantity is measured. EA=Each, CS=Case, PL=Pallet, KG=Kilogram, LB=Pound, L=Liter, GAL=Gallon, M=Meter, FT=Foot. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EA|CS|PL|KG|LB|L|GAL|M|FT — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
The date and time when this stock valuation record was first created in the system.
The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code in which the valuation amounts are expressed (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).
Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Valuation entries are posted to GL accounts; linking enables automated posting and audit.
Reference to the SKU being valued in this record.
The predetermined cost per unit set by the cost accounting team, used for standard costing valuation method.
Unique identifier for the stock valuation record. Primary key.
The base unit of measure for the quantity (e.g., EA for each, KG for kilogram, L for liter).
The date on which this inventory valuation snapshot was taken. Typically aligned with financial period close dates.
The accounting method used to calculate inventory value: standard cost, moving average price, FIFO (First In First Out), weighted average, or LIFO (Last In First Out).
The split valuation type used when a material is valuated separately (e.g., own production vs. external procurement, domestic vs. import).
City where the warehouse is located.
Three‑letter ISO country code of the warehouse location.
Timestamp when the warehouse record was first created in the system.
Geographic latitude coordinate of the warehouse.
Geographic longitude coordinate of the warehouse.
Postal/ZIP code for the warehouse address.
Timestamp of the most recent update to the warehouse record.

Critical for executive and legal visibility into regulatory risk.

Tracks new, amended, or repealed regulations and standards that may impact the company's products or operations. Captures change source (regulatory authority, industry body), change type (new regulation, amendment, repeal, guidance update), affected product categories, affected jurisdictions, impact assessment status, required action deadline, responsible regulatory affairs owner, and implementation status. Drives proactive regulatory intelligence and ensures timely compliance adaptation.

Transactional records documenting compliance assessments against specific regulatory requirements (CFR, IFRA, EU CLP, REACH, state regulations) for each product, formulation, or facility. Captures regulatory framework, specific requirement reference, compliance assessment date, assessor, compliance finding (compliant, non-compliant, conditional), corrective action required, corrective action due date, closure date, and evidence document reference. Supports multi-framework compliance verification including FDA/EPA audit readiness and IFRA fragrance safety substantiation. SSOT for all regulatory compliance assessments regardless of governing body.

Master record of regulatory compliance obligations applicable to the business by jurisdiction, product category, and governing body. Tracks obligation type (registration, labeling, reporting, testing, notification, renewal), governing regulation (CFR part, EU directive, REACH article, state law), applicable product categories, compliance deadline, renewal frequency, advance notice period, responsible regulatory affairs owner, estimated compliance cost, and current compliance status. Drives the regulatory compliance calendar and proactive renewal management.

CPSC (Consumer Product Safety Commission) filing records for mandatory incident reports, Section 15(b) substantial product hazard reports, and SaferProducts.gov submissions. Captures filing type, filing date, CPSC case number, product involved, hazard description, injury/incident details, population at risk, corrective action proposed, and CPSC response received. Tracks compliance with CPSA reporting obligations.

Regulatory dossier master record representing the compiled technical and scientific documentation package supporting a product registration or submission. Tracks dossier type (CTD, eCTD, IECIC, CPNP), version, compilation date, owning regulatory affairs team, completeness status, linked submission, and document repository reference in Veeva Vault. One dossier may support multiple submissions across jurisdictions.

EPA pesticide and antimicrobial product registration records under FIFRA (Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act). Captures EPA registration number, product name, active ingredient(s), registration type (new, amendment, renewal, cancellation), registration date, expiry date, use classification (general/restricted), label approval status, and data call-in requirements. Applicable to household disinfectants, insecticides, and antimicrobial cleaning products.

IFRA (International Fragrance Association) compliance records for fragrance-containing products. Tracks IFRA standard version, fragrance ingredient, product category (leave-on, rinse-off, fine fragrance), maximum permitted usage level per IFRA standard, actual formulated usage level, compliance status (compliant/non-compliant), assessment date, and assessor. Required for fragrance safety substantiation in personal care and household products.

Ingredient declaration records capturing the full ingredient list for a finished product SKU as required for labeling compliance. Tracks INCI names, CAS numbers, concentration ranges, function (preservative, surfactant, fragrance, colorant), declaration order, jurisdiction-specific requirements (FDA 21 CFR, EU Cosmetics Regulation, REACH), allergen flags, and restricted substance flags. Links to product master and formulation records.

Reference master for regulatory jurisdictions defining the geographic and legal scope of regulatory requirements. Captures jurisdiction code, jurisdiction name, country/region, applicable regulatory framework (FDA, EU, ASEAN, GCC), market entry requirement type, language requirements for labeling, and notification vs. registration requirement flag. Used to drive multi-jurisdictional compliance workflows across registrations, labels, and submissions.

Product label version master tracking all approved and historical label artwork versions for each SKU across markets. Captures label version number, market/country, language, label type (primary, secondary, shipper), regulatory approval status, approval date, approving authority, label claims, warning statements, net content declaration, country-of-origin, and Veeva Vault document reference. Supports multi-jurisdictional labeling compliance.

became.before: Product recall and market withdrawal master records initiated voluntarily or mandated by regulatory authorities. SSOT for recall event management across all jurisdictions and authorities.

EU REACH regulation substance master tracking all chemical substances used in products or processes that are subject to REACH registration, evaluation, authorization, or restriction. Captures SVHC (Substance of Very High Concern) status, REACH registration number, EC number, CAS number, tonnage band, authorization status, restriction conditions, SDS requirement flag, and downstream user notification obligations. Critical for EU market access.

Master record of approved and pending regulatory claims for products including structure/function claims, environmental claims (biodegradable, recyclable), organic/natural certifications, and efficacy claims. Prevents unapproved claims from appearing on labels or marketing materials.

Master record for product registrations with regulatory authorities across all jurisdictions. Tracks registration number, status, effective/expiry dates, registering authority, product scope, registration type (new, renewal, amendment, cancellation), active ingredients, use classification, submission reference, and renewal due date.
